rgb: This outdoor scene takes place on pavement beside a grassy edge on the left. The camera wearer is facing a black metal A-frame trailer tongue positioned 0.3 to 0.7 metres ahead of and below the camera, hitched between the rear bumper of a tow vehicle on the left, roughly 0.5 to 0.8 metres away, and a wooden-deck trailer bed on the right. In frame one, the wearer’s right hand is resting within arm’s reach on the trailer’s front rail. Another person’s lower legs are partly visible about 3 metres away near the trailer bed’s upper-left edge, while the remainder of their body is cut off above the frame. During frames two and three, the wearer rotates slightly left, angles the view more sharply downward, and uses both hands from 0.4 to 0.6 metres away to raise the triangular metal toolbox lid from left to right, revealing previously hidden coiled grey straps and metal chains. In frame four, the wearer’s left hand holds a coiled strap in the open box’s left corner as a second person comes from the upper left to within 0.6 to 0.9 metres of the wearer and 0.3 to 0.5 metres of the toolbox. By frame five, that second person, dressed in a red shirt and jeans and facing right toward both the toolbox and wearer, has moved to about 0.5 to 0.7 metres from the wearer. Their head and upper torso remain beyond the upper-left border, making their gaze unobservable, while their right hand reaches the same strap held by the wearer’s left hand within arm’s reach. The tow vehicle and trailer bed are still mostly cut off along the left and right borders.
depth: The depth visualization presents a downward egocentric perspective, with the camera wearer standing immediately over a triangular trailer-tongue toolbox approximately 0.6–1.0 m beneath their head. The toolbox is connected to a vehicle bumper on the left and a wooden trailer bed on the right, while the asphalt lies around 1.5–1.7 m below. The brightest areas correspond to the wearer’s torso and shoulders along the bottom border, 0.2–0.4 m away, together with their arms reaching downward within arm’s reach, at 0.5–0.8 m, to raise the toolbox lid in frames 2–3 and take hold of a coiled strap inside during frames 4–5. A second person is only faintly present at the upper left in frame 1, about 2.5–3.0 m distant. They advance from that direction in frame 4, when a hand enters at approximately 0.8 m, and reach into the box in frame 5, sitting 0.5–0.9 m from the wearer and roughly 0.3 m from the wearer’s left hand. This person is turned sideways toward the toolbox, with their head and upper torso outside the crop. Relative to the RGB sequence, the depth output cleanly distinguishes the foreground raised lid, upright jack post, and overhanging torso from the lower ground surface, unaffected by black paint or deep shadows. Inside the open toolbox in frames 3–5, however, it is unreliable: the intertwined straps and chains merge into a vague mid-grey mass. Fine depth breaks are also missing along the slender hitch chains.
segmentation: Throughout all five frames, the segmentation output traces the camera wearer’s lower torso, legs, and arms at the bottom, 0.2–0.8 m away and oriented forward and downward toward the trailer tongue. It also marks the second person coming in from the upper left during frames 4 and 5, at 0.5–1.2 m away, standing left of the toolbox and reaching rightward into its compartment within the wearer’s arm’s reach. Over the sequence, the wearer’s segmented left arm moves forward to raise the triangular lid in frame 2, then extends into the opened compartment across frames 3–5. Meanwhile, the second person’s arm and bent legs appear through the top-left boundary in frames 4–5 as they take hold of the same strap. Although these masks make it easier to separate the two people’s overlapping limbs at the lower and left borders from the dark pavement, object identification and boundary accuracy are highly unreliable. In frame 1, the system incorrectly identifies the trailer bed and tongue as an ‘airplane’; in frame 2, it calls the triangular metal toolbox an ‘umbrella’; and in frames 3 and 5, it assigns ‘person’ masks to the raised toolbox lid and the chains and straps inside. It also misses the trailer, hitch, and toolbox entirely in frame 4, rendering every non-person part of the scene black.
pose: Only magenta three-dimensional hand skeletons appear in the pose output’s first three frames. No yellow body skeleton is shown in any of the five frames, since the downward-facing view largely excludes both individuals’ heads and complete bodies. Frame 1 registers the camera wearer’s right hand resting on the trailer frame at the bottom right, approximately 0.6 m away. In frames 2 and 3, it follows both wearer hands: the left hand is at centre-left and 0.6–0.7 m distant, while the right is at centre-right and 0.5–0.7 m distant, with about 0.3–0.4 m between them. The hands grasp the toolbox latch and hold the lid open within easy reach. Compared with the strongly contrasted RGB image, this skeleton display makes the wearer’s precise finger positions and pinch grip in frames 1–3 more legible, particularly where the frame-2 left hand overlaps dark metal. The pose output becomes wholly unreliable in frames 4 and 5, producing completely black images and detecting neither hands nor bodies, even though the wearer’s hands and the approaching second person’s left arm and legs are plainly visible while interacting with the strap from 0.5–1.0 m away.
